---
title: "Authorship attribution"
---

Quarto can surface per-node authorship information in rendered output,
sourcing it from `git blame` on the command line or from the Automerge
edit history inside the hub-client. The feature is **opt-in**: nothing
is emitted unless you ask for it.

## Privacy and discoverability

Attribution writes author email addresses (or display names supplied
by the producer) into the rendered HTML. **Anyone with access to the
output can read them** — and they survive as `data-attr-*` attributes
even on static hosts, including those served by GitHub Pages, Netlify,
or behind a CDN. Treat the rendered output as having the same
exposure surface as a public commit log.

If that's not the right tradeoff for a given project, leave attribution
off. The CLI and YAML defaults are both off; there is no implicit
enablement.

## Enabling attribution on the command line

Pass `--attribution=git` when invoking `quarto render`:

```bash
quarto render report.qmd --attribution=git
```

Quarto shells out to `git blame --porcelain` for the input file,
maps each line to an author email and commit timestamp, and emits the
result on every wrapped node in the rendered HTML.

To turn attribution off explicitly — for example when overriding a
YAML default — use `--attribution=off`.

## Enabling attribution via YAML

The same setting is available in document YAML:

```yaml
---
title: My report
attribution: git
---
```

The two values supported in v1 are `git` (run the `git blame`
provider) and `off` (no attribution, identical to the default).

### CLI overrides YAML

When the CLI flag and document YAML disagree, the CLI wins. This
makes `--attribution=off` a reliable escape hatch even on documents
that opt in by default:

| `--attribution` | YAML `attribution` | Effective mode |
|---|---|---|
| (unset)         | (unset)            | off            |
| (unset)         | `off`              | off            |
| (unset)         | `git`              | git            |
| `off`           | (unset)            | off            |
| `off`           | `git`              | **off** (CLI wins) |
| `git`           | (unset)            | git            |
| `git`           | `off`              | **git** (CLI wins) |
| `git`           | `git`              | git            |

### Supplying custom display names

The `git` provider derives a display name and colour from each
author's email automatically (mail-local-part plus a deterministic
HSL colour). If you want different labels — for instance to spell out
"Alice Cooper" instead of `alice` — override them in YAML:

```yaml
---
title: My report
attribution:
  source: git
  identities:
    alice@example.com:
      display_name: "Alice Cooper"
      color: "#c0392b"
    bob@example.com:
      display_name: "Bob Roberts"
---
```

User identity entries are merged on top of provider-supplied ones:
a key present in both takes the YAML value. Keys present **only** in
YAML are dropped — overrides are matched against actors the provider
actually reports, so a stale entry can't silently inject a phantom
author.

## What attribution looks like in the output

Each wrapping `<span>` carries four data attributes:

```html
<span
  data-attr-actor="alice@example.com"
  data-attr-time="1700000000000"
  data-attr-name="alice"
  data-attr-color="hsl(253, 60%, 55%)">
  …
</span>
```

- `data-attr-actor` — the raw actor identifier (the author email for
  `git`, an Automerge actor ID inside the hub).
- `data-attr-time` — Unix epoch timestamp of the most recent commit
  (or edit) touching the wrapped range. The `git` provider emits
  **seconds**; the hub-client (Automerge) emits **milliseconds**.
  Consumers that handle both should use a threshold like `< 1e12` to
  tell them apart.
- `data-attr-name` — a human-friendly display name.
- `data-attr-color` — a deterministic CSS colour.

Contiguous prose authored by the same actor at the same time
coalesces into a single outer wrapper, so a paragraph written by one
person produces one wrapper rather than one per word. Structured
inlines (links, code, math, etc.) always get their own wrapper.

Styling is left to the consuming theme; use the `data-attr-color`
attribute or a CSS rule keyed off `data-attr-actor` to colour
authored regions however you like.

## Adding a viewer overlay {#viewer-overlay}

The data attributes above are inert. A static HTML page rendered with
`--attribution=git` looks identical to one rendered without it until
something styles the data — a site theme, a custom Pandoc filter, or
the small overlay below.

The snippet that follows reproduces the floating badge the
[hub-client](#hub-client-integration) shows under its **Authorship**
toggle, so a published `.html` file and a live hub session feel the
same on hover. The class names (`q2-attr-badge`,
`q2-attr-badge-dot`, `q2-attr-badge-time`) match the hub-client's,
so a site theme that styles them once works in both places.

Save the following as `attribution-viewer.css`:

```css
[data-attr-actor] {
    text-decoration: underline dotted;
    text-underline-offset: 4px;
    cursor: help;
}

.q2-attr-badge {
    display: inline-block;
    z-index: 10;
    font-size: 10px;
    line-height: 1;
    white-space: nowrap;
    padding: 2px 6px;
    border-radius: 3px;
    background: #fff;
    border: 1px solid var(--attr-color);
    color: var(--attr-color);
    font-weight: 600;
    pointer-events: none;
}
.q2-attr-badge-dot {
    display: inline-block;
    width: 6px;
    height: 6px;
    border-radius: 50%;
    margin-right: 3px;
    vertical-align: middle;
}
.q2-attr-badge-time {
    font-weight: 400;
    opacity: 0.7;
}
```

And the following as `attribution-viewer.js`:

```js
function formatRelativeTime(timestamp) {
    const now = Date.now();
    // git blame emits seconds, Automerge emits milliseconds;
    // the 1e12 threshold distinguishes them.
    const tsMs = timestamp < 1e12 ? timestamp * 1000 : timestamp;
    const diffSec = Math.floor((now - tsMs) / 1000);
    if (diffSec < 60) return 'just now';
    const diffMin = Math.floor(diffSec / 60);
    if (diffMin < 60) return `${diffMin}m ago`;
    const diffHr = Math.floor(diffMin / 60);
    if (diffHr < 24) return `${diffHr}h ago`;
    const diffDay = Math.floor(diffHr / 24);
    return `${diffDay}d ago`;
}

// Paint each attributed element in its author's colour so descendants
// inherit it via the cascade.
document.querySelectorAll('[data-attr-actor]').forEach((el) => {
    const color = el.getAttribute('data-attr-color');
    if (color) {
        el.style.color = color;
        el.style.textDecorationColor = color;
    }
});

function buildBadge(leaf) {
    const name = leaf.getAttribute('data-attr-name');
    const color = leaf.getAttribute('data-attr-color');
    const time = Number(leaf.getAttribute('data-attr-time'));
    if (!name || !color || !Number.isFinite(time)) return null;

    const badge = document.createElement('span');
    badge.className = 'q2-attr-badge';
    badge.style.setProperty('--attr-color', color);

    const dot = document.createElement('span');
    dot.className = 'q2-attr-badge-dot';
    dot.style.backgroundColor = color;
    badge.appendChild(dot);

    badge.appendChild(document.createTextNode(`${name} `));

    const timeEl = document.createElement('span');
    timeEl.className = 'q2-attr-badge-time';
    timeEl.textContent = formatRelativeTime(time);
    badge.appendChild(timeEl);

    return badge;
}

let currentBadge = null;

document.addEventListener('mouseover', (e) => {
    const leaf = e.target.closest('[data-attr-actor]');
    if (!leaf) return;
    if (currentBadge) currentBadge.remove();

    const badge = buildBadge(leaf);
    if (!badge) return;

    const rect = leaf.getBoundingClientRect();
    badge.style.position = 'fixed';
    badge.style.top = `${rect.bottom + 2}px`;
    badge.style.left = `${rect.left}px`;

    document.body.appendChild(badge);
    currentBadge = badge;
});

document.addEventListener('mouseout', (e) => {
    const related = e.relatedTarget;
    if (related && related.closest && related.closest('[data-attr-actor]')) {
        return;
    }
    if (currentBadge) {
        currentBadge.remove();
        currentBadge = null;
    }
});
```

Wire both files into the document via YAML. The CSS goes in directly;
the JS is referenced from a short HTML shim
(`attribution-viewer-include.html`) containing a single line —
`<script src="attribution-viewer.js"></script>`:

```yaml
---
title: My report
attribution: git
format:
  html:
    css: attribution-viewer.css
    include-after-body: attribution-viewer-include.html
    resources:
      - attribution-viewer.js
---
```

The `resources:` entry ensures the `.js` file is copied next to the
rendered HTML so the `<script src=…>` reference resolves at runtime.

The snippet is intentionally small and dependency-free — copy it into
a site theme, adapt it to taste, or strip it back to just the CSS if
you don't need the hover badge. The four `data-attr-*` attributes are
the stable contract; everything above is presentation.

## Hub-client integration

The Quarto hub client ships the same attribution data path,
sourcing actors from the Automerge edit history of the live document
rather than from `git blame`. The data wire is in place; the
in-product toggle and renderer-side colouring are still in
development — when they land, an "Authorship" control will appear in
the document settings.

## Current limits

- **Single-document blame only.** Content spliced in via
  `{{< include other.qmd >}}` is not attributed in v1; the wrappers
  for included nodes will be absent. A future release will extend
  blame across the entire include chain.
- **No caching.** Each render re-runs `git blame`. On a 100 K-line
  file this completes in roughly 50 ms, so caching is not currently a
  bottleneck.
- **No project-wide aggregation.** Each document's attribution is
  scoped to that document; cross-document summaries ("Alice
  contributed to N pages") are a future feature.
